`final class SignalContext`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.signal` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [SignalContext.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/signal/SignalContext.java)

Per-thread state of the signal engine: batches, silence, read tracking and the queue of notifications.

## Description

Each thread has its own `SignalContext`, which [`Signal`](/reference/signals/signal/) and [`ComputedSignal`](/reference/signals/computedsignal/) use to record reads, group notifications and defer writes made outside the render thread.
Application code uses `Signal.batch(...)` and `Signal.silent(...)` instead.

<a id="SignalContext-method-open"></a>

### open

`void open()` 

Opens a batch: notifications wait until the matching `close()`.

<a id="SignalContext-method-close"></a>

### close

`void close()` 

**Thread:** runs on the render thread.

Closes a batch; at the outermost level, it sends the deferred writes to the render thread and delivers the notifications.
When listeners throw, the others still run and the first exception is thrown at the end.

<a id="SignalContext-method-getEpoch"></a>

### getEpoch

`long getEpoch()` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Returns the global change counter, which grows on every change of any signal.

<a id="SignalContext-method-countWriteBack"></a>

### countWriteBack

`int countWriteBack(Signal<?> signal)` 

Counts the writes back to `signal` during the delivery in progress and returns the count; it returns `0` outside a delivery.
Bound controls use it to stop two controls that keep correcting each other.

### getWriteBackOrigin

<a id="SignalContext-method-defer"></a>

### defer

`void defer(Runnable task)` 

**Thread:** runs on the render thread.

Queues a write for the render thread: at the end of the batch inside a batch, otherwise at once.
The write keeps the silence of the code that queued it.
